value.description: The registered payload schema DOCUMENT for fact2 relation payloads, named by identity-and-evidence section 3 and native-evidence section 4.4. fact.payloadSchemaDigest is the raw SHA-256 of the EXACT FULL BYTES of this file; validation uses the selector the payload registry row names, exactly as the native and workflow import registries already work. This document has no root type on purpose: it is a multi-record bundle, and a bundle is admitted through its registry row, never by validating a payload against the whole document. ENCODING SUCCESSOR: fact2 payloads are canonical JSON C, not the inherited deterministic-CBOR profile. Every logical restriction that profile carried survives here as an admission rule - NFC text, no negative integers, closed field sets, enums, per-rung required/forbidden fields and the universe rule. Historical FactRecord1 CBOR bytes and their provenance are unchanged and remain valid history; they are never a fact2 preimage.

x-opensip-relation-registry.standing: Normative. Closed at 13 relations: the twelve inherited from fact-plane.v1 relationPayloadSchemaRegistryV1 plus native-evidence section 4.4 unresolved-edge.
x-opensip-relation-registry.payloadSchemaDigest: raw SHA-256 of the exact full bytes of that file
x-opensip-relation-registry.ladderAuthority: This registry is the SINGLE authority for every relation's resolution ladder, as identity-and-evidence section 3 states. `ladder` is that relation's total order over its OWN resolution methods, listed weakest-first, inherited verbatim from fact-plane.v1 relationRegistry.relations[].ladder (plus [observed] for unresolved-edge). Every other copy in the kit - native_evidence_model.v2.py LADDERS and capability-manifest-domains.v2.json RELATION-LADDER-DOMAIN-V2.ladders - is a declared MIRROR of this array and is drift-checked against it exactly and IN ORDER. A one-rung ladder is not a deficiency; it means the relation is fully determined at that rung.
x-opensip-relation-registry.rungsAreFieldRulesNotTheLadder: `rungs` is a different table: the per-rung required/forbidden PAYLOAD FIELD rules. It is legitimately the empty object for a relation with no per-rung field variance, which is every single-rung relation. Reading `rungs` as the ladder is the defect this key exists to prevent: an empty field-rule table must never be read as an absent ladder, and never as a licence to skip ladder membership. Membership is checked against `ladder`, always, with no fallback.
x-opensip-relation-registry.membershipRule: A resolution is admissible for a relation only if it is a member of THAT relation's `ladder`. A rung that is a member of another relation's ladder is refused, not accepted as a live vocabulary token; the flat rung vocabulary published elsewhere is necessary but never sufficient. Order comparison is the index within one relation's ladder; nothing orders a rung of one relation against a rung of another, and there is no global rank.
x-opensip-relation-registry.subjectKindLaw: What a subject-scope's `subjects` entries IDENTIFY, per relation. `source-path`: each subject is a path in the snapshot this scope names, so the scope's own extent is exactly those paths - `file` and `vcs-change` bind it through their registry snapshotJoins pathField, and `clones` binds it through bodyIdentityJoin, whose single anchor IS the body span the identity is over. `package-name`: a package identifier, not a path. `symbol`: an opaque SubjectIdV1 that the record associates with no path; the enumerator's attribution of symbols to files is trusted and is NOT re-derivable from the retained Run, so no per-subject path law is possible for these relations and any capability question about them can only be answered at the coarser retained extent. That limit is stated rather than worked around: inventing symbol-to-path parsing would be fabricated evidence.

anchorLaw.standing: Normative and CLOSED. Every relation row carries an `anchorLaw`; there is no default and no unstated relation. It decides how many `fact.anchors` entries a fact of that relation carries, and therefore whether one semantic input has one spelling or several.
anchorLaw.whyThisIsARegistryLaw: `fact.anchors` is `minItems`-free in the identity schema and only `clones` ever stated a cardinality. Every predicate written over the array - the `file` row's `anchorPathField`, and native-evidence section 1.2's `every one of its anchor paths` - is universally quantified, so at ZERO anchors it is vacuously TRUE and neither permits nor forbids that spelling. On the frozen v13 reference BOTH the whole-file-anchored and the unanchored spelling of one `file@enumerated` claim close a Run, with DIFFERENT fact2 identities (`5cce76d9...` and `d7bb2235...` over `tool/main.py`). A universally quantified predicate over an array of unstated length is not a closed law; the cardinality has to be stated.

source-text.rule: A code fact is READ FROM SOURCE TEXT, so it must name at least one anchor: the span it was read from. An unanchored code fact names no file that could have been read and is refused (`FACT_ANCHOR_CARDINALITY`). This was previously enforced only inside the syntax-universe capability guard, so the same unanchored `declares` or `references` fact closed a Run under a TypeScript or Rust universe; the law is one law and now binds in every universe.
source-text.noIdentityEqualityPromise: There is deliberately NO ADDITIONAL relation-specific maximum and no canonical extent BEYOND THE COMMON SCHEMA BOUNDS - foundation fact.anchors already carries maxItems 100000 and uniqueItems, and those continue to apply to every relation. An earlier revision said there is no upper bound at all, which contradicted that global bound; what this class declines to impose is a per-relation ceiling or a canonical span set, not the shared one. Which spans a producer cites for a multi-span claim is a genuine semantic choice about what was read, so two conformant producers that cite different spans have produced DIFFERENT semantic descriptors and legitimately mint different fact2 identities. Nothing here promises cross-provider anchor identity for code facts, and asserting one would be a false equality between two different pieces of evidence.

body-identity.rule: Unchanged from the existing `bodyIdentityJoin.anchorCardinality`: exactly the body span the identity is over. Zero would leave the claim unattached and several would make the L0 recomputation a choice.

inventory.rule: An inventory fact is NOT read from a source span. Its whole semantic input is its payload, and that payload is already bound to the snapshot by this relation's own `snapshotJoins`: the path must be in the snapshot inventory, and for `file` the content digest, the byte length and CUSTODY of the exact retained bytes are joined as well. An anchor could only restate a subset of a claim that is already joined, and because nothing derives it, it is a free axis that gives one semantic input several spellings and several identities. It is therefore closed at zero (`FACT_ANCHOR_CARDINALITY`).
inventory.whatThisMakesRepresentable: Exactly zero is the only cardinality every inventoried path can satisfy, which is what makes the unconditional inventory promise honest: a path no bundled grammar reads (`tool/main.py`), an extensionless path (`LICENSE`), a data-document path, and - decisively - a `vcs-change` whose `changeKind` is `deleted`, whose path is by construction NOT in the analysed snapshot and can therefore carry no anchor at all. A cardinality of one would make that last case unrepresentable and would newly require the manifest bytes of every `package` fact to be retained, neither of which any contract asks for.
inventory.whatItAlsoCloses: The `file` row's `anchorPathField` was the only defence against an arbitrary anchor borrowed to satisfy an inventory claim, and it covered `file` alone: on frozen v13 a `package@manifest-declared` fact claiming `package.json` closed a Run while anchored into an unrelated `a.ts`. Closing the class at zero refuses that for all three inventory relations with one reason. `anchorPathField` is retained as the narrower per-row statement it always was; under this cardinality it can no longer be reached for `file`, and that is the point - the broader law subsumes it rather than leaving a predicate whose only remaining reading is the vacuous one.
inventory.rawByteBoundary: An inventory claim retains path, content digest and byte length WITHOUT anyone decoding the bytes. At zero anchors the ANCHOR_SOURCE/ANCHOR_RANGE/ANCHOR_UTF8 checks never run for such a fact - they iterate the anchors - while the inventoried-file join still does, and it only hashes and measures. An EMPTY file and a NON-UTF8 BINARY file are therefore ordinary inventory, at an extensionless path as readily as any other; requiring bytes to parse as code or as UTF8 merely to record their path and hash would narrow the promise. The source-text and body-identity classes keep exactly the scope they had: the SAME non-UTF8 bytes still refuse as a code-span anchor (ANCHOR_UTF8), and the digest, length and path joins still refuse a wrong claim about those bytes.
inventory.locationRouteAfterRemovingAnchors: Removing inventory anchors removes NO location route, and none is invented to replace them. Nothing reads fact.anchors as a finding location: a finding locates through finding-fingerprint.subjectKey.logicalPath, an inventory claim's own location is its payload path joined to the snapshot inventory by this relation's snapshotJoins, and finding, finding-fingerprint, proof-bundle and predicate-witness carry no anchor field at all. A finding over a zero-anchor inventory fact closes a Run and is located by exactly those existing records.

anchorLaw.notAGrammarQuestion: Anchor cardinality and syntax-universe capability are different laws and neither substitutes for the other. The grammar-capability registry decides which relation@rung a SELECTED grammar can bear; this law decides how many spans a fact of that relation cites. Inventory capabilities are ungated by grammar at BOTH enforcement boundaries (see the native grammar-capability registry `enforcementBoundaries`), and independently carry no anchors at all.
anchorLaw.enforcedAt: The producer must enforce this law on every owning fact, and the verifier must enforce it again at retained Run closure. The reference model exhibits the latter through identity-model relation_payload_rules inside open_run_closure; it does not exhibit a separate producer-boundary call site. Producer enforcement remains an implementation conformance obligation. At retained Run closure it is checked before the relation's snapshot joins, so the cardinality fault is reported as itself rather than as a downstream join failure.

coverageTotalityLaw.standing: Normative and CLOSED. A relation row carries a `coverageTotality` row only where the relation's own meaning makes its rung TOTAL over the snapshot inventory. A relation with no row declares that a subject may lawfully bear no fact, which is itself the record that nothing further constrains it.
coverageTotalityLaw.whyItIsNeeded: `entry.coverage: complete` is a claim that the committed examined partition was examined exhaustively. For a rung that is total over the inventory that claim also decides a universal negative: over a COMPLETE `file@enumerated` Coverage, `exists file where path=P` is authoritative, so a complete result that retains no fact for an inventoried subject asserts that an inventoried file is ABSENT. On frozen v13 that graph closed - a `file@enumerated` scope over the inventoried subject `a.ts`, `coverage: complete`, `deficiency: null` and zero facts. Nothing derived the obligation, so nothing refused it.
coverageTotalityLaw.whichRelationsHaveOne: `file@enumerated` only. A snapshot inventories exactly the files it contains, so every inventoried path has exactly one file fact and an omission is an error. `package@manifest-declared` and `vcs-change@vcs-reported` are NOT total and get no row: most paths declare no package and most paths were not changed, so their empty results are ordinary findings rather than omissions. Applying totality to them would manufacture obligations the relations do not carry.
coverageTotalityLaw.whatItDoesNotRequire: Only subjects that are IN the snapshot inventory are owed a fact. A scope naming a path the snapshot does not contain is answered honestly by a complete result with no fact for it - the host examined the question and the file is genuinely absent. And the law is conditional on `coverage: complete`: an `unknown` result with its disclosed deficiency owes nothing, which is what keeps a partially examined inventory representable.
coverageTotalityLaw.enforcedAt: identity-model close_run, over the RETAINED view's own facts and the retained snapshot inventory, alongside the other Coverage prerequisites. It reads no claimed value except the `complete` it is judging.

coveragePartitionLaw.standing: Normative and CLOSED. The DISJOINTNESS half of identity-and-evidence section 3's `Coverage scopes partition the claimed universe without overlaps or omissions`. The OMISSION half is coverageTotalityLaw above and is owed only where a relation carries a coverageTotality row. These two halves have different owners and different decidability, and neither implies the other.
coveragePartitionLaw.whyItIsNeeded: The clause was stated and nothing derived or compared it. A retained Run could carry two subject-scopes of ONE view with the same snapshot, relation, rung and both universes whose subject sets intersect, and close. What that demonstrates is that an INVALID partition was ACCEPTED: the same subject was committed twice under one interpretation, so a claim read over that view - a count, a completeness claim or a universal negative - can be ambiguous or double-counted depending on how a consumer joins the scopes. It is NOT asserted that every consumer necessarily double-counts; what is established, and what this law fixes, is that the published partition property was not decided anywhere. That is the same defect class as the frozen-reference file@enumerated omission.
coveragePartitionLaw.keyRule: Two subject-scopes of the same view are in the same partition exactly when they agree on EVERY field of partitionKey. Within one partition their `subjects` arrays must be pairwise disjoint. Scopes in DIFFERENT partitions may name the same subject freely: a different relation, a different rung or a different universe is a different claim about that subject, not an overlap. This is the same tuple coverageTotalityLaw uses for `matchOn`, deliberately, so the key that decides which fact discharges a scope's obligation is the key that decides which scopes are comparable at all.
coveragePartitionLaw.snapshotIsListedDeliberately: Run closure independently requires every subject-scope to carry the Run's own snapshotId, so within one admitted Run this field is constant and listing it changes no outcome today. It is listed for the same reason coverageTotalityLaw lists it: this law reads a property of a SHARED view, and a join that silently depends on an invariant enforced elsewhere is the implicit coupling both laws exist to remove.
coveragePartitionLaw.scope: PER VIEW, over every subject-scope the view references - INCLUDING scopes that carry no Coverage entry. A scope with no Coverage bypasses the per-Coverage PRODUCER guard (admit_coverage_result_v3 is never called for it), which is exactly the case a single-Coverage producer cannot decide; it does still reach the retained-scope ladder guard (SUBJECT_SCOPE_RUNG_NOT_IN_RELATION_LADDER) later in close_run, so saying it reaches no other check at all would be false. Distinct views of one Run may reference the SAME scope, and that is not an overlap: a view is one producer's interpretation, and the partition is a property of that interpretation.
whatRemainsAllowed: the same scope referenced by two different views of one Run
the same subject in two scopes that differ on any partitionKey field
a scope with no Coverage entry, which is still partitioned
lawful partial, not-attempted and unknown Coverage states, which this law does not read
coveragePartitionLaw.producerCannotDecideThis: admit_coverage_result_v3 admits ONE scope and its ONE Coverage entry and cannot see a second scope, so it cannot decide a between-scopes property and is not asked to. The authoritative boundary is retained Run closure, which holds the whole view. No host effect, provider call or protocol invocation is introduced by this law.
coveragePartitionLaw.refusalShape: SUBJECT_SCOPE_PARTITION_OVERLAP:<relation>@<rung>:<lowest overlapping subject by UTF-8 BYTE order>, matching the COVERAGE_INVENTORY_TOTALITY_OMITS_PATH shape. The ordering is named exactly: it is the byte order of the subject's UTF-8 encoding, the same order the x-opensip-order `utf8` vocabulary names, and it is NOT the canonical-JSON encoded order, which escapes and quotes and can differ. Only which subject is REPORTED depends on it; whether the Run refuses does not. It is an internal admission refusal: no public DomainDetailCode and no D9 class, exit or error code is added or changed.
coveragePartitionLaw.enforcedAt: identity-model close_run, per view, AFTER each scope's own well-formedness checks (SCOPE_SOURCE_JOIN, UNSELECTED_ENUMERATOR, ENUMERATOR_CLOSURE_KIND) have run for every scope of that view, so a malformed scope refuses as ITSELF and the overlap refusal is never counted as coverage of a different fault. The key is READ from partitionKey here, never restated in code.

bodyIdentityJoin.levelSpecificationRetained: normalisationVersion names the retained level specification bytes
bodyIdentityJoin.note: At L0 the canonical payload is the raw body-span bytes, so the host recomputes it from the enclosing fact anchor: a real source join. At L1-L3 it is a versioned normalizer output the host cannot recompute, so the requirement is exact retained preimage custody plus the framed-identity check. This is custody and framing evidence; it qualifies no normalizer.
bodyIdentityJoin.anchorRule: A clones fact carries exactly one anchor: the body span the identity is over. Zero anchors would leave the claim unattached and several would make the L0 recomputation a choice, which is the arbitrary-anchor defect in another form. `anchorCardinality` here is a declared MIRROR of this relation's registry `anchorLaw` (class `body-identity`, cardinality 1), which is the single enforcing statement and is applied to every relation before any payload join runs. The join checks that the two AGREE (`RELATION_ANCHOR_LAW_DRIFT`) rather than refusing the same fault a second time under a second name.
bodyIdentityJoin.languageIdSource: the BODY's language, from the SAME selector over the SAME single anchor that produces the body dialect: the `languageVersionBinding` of the fact sourceUniverse domain registry row, where `dialect.form` is `closed-suffix-table` gives `bodyLanguageByVariant[<the variant that table selects from this anchor's path suffix, longest match wins>]`, and any other dialect form gives `bodyLanguage`. The value is always a member of that row's `bodyLanguages` and of the closed foundation `#/$defs/body-language-version` `languageId` enum {javascript, rust, typescript}.
bodyIdentityJoin.languageIdIsNotTheProviderLanguage: It is emphatically NOT the domain row's own `language` field. That field names the ENGINE that read the body, and the two differ in both live cases: a `.js` body under `native.semantic-universe.typescript.v2` is a `javascript` body, not `typescript`, and every body under `native.semantic-universe.syntax.v2` would read as `syntax`, which the closed languageId enum does not contain, so a literal implementer would mint a different clone identity for every JavaScript body and NO admissible identity at all under the syntax universe. An earlier revision of this key said `the language of the fact sourceUniverse domain registry row`, which is that wrong reading; identity-and-evidence section 3 and each domain row's own `bodyLanguageLaw` always said the derived one, and the identity-model body-identity join has always checked the derived projection. This key is now the same sentence as those two.
bodyIdentityJoin.languageVersionSource: the raw 32 bytes of SHA-256(C(body-language-version)), the closed DERIVED record at foundation/identity-schemas.v2.json#/$defs/body-language-version, rebuilt by Run closure from the universe ResolvedInputs and the admitted retained native context the universe own nativeContextId names, per that universe domain languageVersionBinding. It carries the identity of the component that INTERPRETS the body span plus the selected source dialect; it never carries a human display string, an option-synthesis version, an operational platform value, a path, or a whole per-crate map. Fixed width, because the inherited frame gives each component a u8 length.
bodyIdentityJoin.tokenStreamFraming: u32be token_count || token*, token = u16be kind_id_len || kind_id || u32be value_len || value. The closure parses the retained L1-L3 stream to prove custody and framing; it does not and must not judge the tokenisation itself.

coverageTotality.matchLaw: A fact discharges THIS scope's obligation only if it agrees with the scope on EVERY coordinate listed in matchOn. Those are the four CoverageKeyV2 coordinates other than the subject-scope commitment itself, plus the owning snapshot. An earlier revision matched relation and resolution ALONE, and that is not enough in a view that carries more than one universe: the view-level fact/scope join is EXISTENTIAL - each fact must agree with SOME scope on relation, rung and both universes - so a TypeScript file fact is lawfully in a view that also carries a syntax-universe scope, and it then paid that scope's missing-file obligation. A complete Run exhibited exactly that (root diagnostic attempt3: two complete file@enumerated scopes for `a.ts`, only the TypeScript fact, ADMIT). Totality is a claim about what THIS universe examined, so it must be discharged by evidence produced in THIS universe; a fact from another universe is a different interpretation of the same bytes and is not the same observation.

CanonicalText.description: Inherited CanonicalText: non-empty NFC text with no C0/C1 control characters. NFC text is an ADMISSION rule, not an encoder rule: C never normalizes. The host admits a relation payload only when every text value is already NFC, exactly as the inherited deterministic-CBOR profile required, and refuses otherwise.

x-opensip-digest.codec: SHA-256 over the fully framed domain-separated preimage: u8 len||domainTag, u8 len||levelId, u8 len||levelVersion (RAW 32 bytes, not hexadecimal display text), u8 len||languageId, u8 len||languageVersion, u32be len||payload. Unframed concatenation is FORBIDDEN.

payloadEncoding.L0-verbatim: u32be raw_byte_len || exact snapshot body-span bytes; tokenisation forbidden

x-opensip-digest.join: the frame is retained under the 64-hex suffix, so SHA-256(retained frame) equals it; the closure parses the frame and requires domainTag, levelId == normalisationLevel, levelVersion == the RAW 32 digest bytes of normalisationVersion, languageId from the fact sourceUniverse domain row, languageVersion == the RAW 32 digest bytes of the recomputed body-language-version projection, and at L0-verbatim the payload equals the enclosing fact anchor span bytes
x-opensip-digest.neverEquals: FACT-ID-V1. The fact identity wraps the complete clone fact and can never equal or substitute for bodyIdentity, by type or by domain (docs/coop/artifacts/fact-identity-policy.v2.json#/factRecordIdentityBoundaryV1/clonePayloadJoin).

x-opensip-digest.artifact: the exact retained canonical LEVEL SPECIFICATION bytes for this normalisation level: per-language lexical boundary rules, canonical token-kind registry, directive classification, transform order and replacement byte rules
x-opensip-digest.note: A human semantic-version label alone is insufficient, and this is never an opaque caller hash.

x-opensip-digest-law.standing: The closing digest law of identity-and-evidence section 3, extended to this bundle. Every DigestHex, Sha256Text and CanonicalPath field here carries x-opensip-digest naming its representation, producing preimage, codec, retention and owning authority. There is no default and no residue: a new such field added without an annotation is inadmissible. Coverage is asserted by consumed CHECKS in the Run closure, not by counting annotations.

retention.preimage: the exact preimage bytes are retained under this digest and the closure re-hashes them
retention.snapshot-inventoried: the value names a path in the analysed snapshot inventory, joined there
retention.provider-output-retained: the canonical payload is a versioned normalizer output the host cannot recompute; its exact framed preimage is retained so an independent replay can re-hash it
retention.not-joined: the value names a state outside the analysed snapshot and is deliberately joined to nothing; the reason is stated on the field and the closure records the exemption rather than leaving it as residue

x-opensip-digest-law.enforcement: identity-model close_run applies the per-relation snapshotJoins and bodyIdentity joins below to EVERY owning fact, after registered-selector validation and independently of the payload decode cache. A payload alone cannot decide snapshot truth, so the enclosing fact, the snapshot, the retained blobs and the bound native context are required owner context.
x-opensip-digest-law.residueRule: Consumed, not declared. Every x-opensip-digest field of a relation selector must be reachable from that relation registry entry snapshotJoins or bodyIdentityJoin, or must declare retention not-joined with its reason. An annotated field with no join, a join naming a field the selector does not have, and an unannotated digest/path field are each inadmissible.

value.title: Native evidence closed schemas v2 (PROPOSED design reference)
value.description: Closed Draft 2020-12 records for the native evidence contract. Exact typed admission (foundation/canonical.py) precedes validation: integers are exact JSON integer literals, booleans are not integers, no float/exponent/-0, no duplicate keys, no lone surrogates. The import2 wrapper itself is foundation/identity-schemas.v2.json#/$defs/import; these are its native typed payloads plus native context/coverage/protocol records. Revision after Codex review v2: per-language co-located units (WorkspaceUnitV2/UnitMembershipV1), inert generated-file rows with a read-only virtual OUT_DIR, workflow canonical import payloads with native adapter-input shapes, ImportRegistryRowV1, preparedResolution, principal join, StageAuthorityV1. Blind-consumer corrections: the closed TypeScript native context (TypeScriptNativeContextV2 and family, domain native.context.typescript.v2, carrying typescriptStdlibMerkleRoot) and the subject-scope commitment / coverage-admission records.

x-opensip-deficiency-cause-registry.standing: Normative and CLOSED. For every DeficiencyV2 member, WHICH retained field carries its cause and what that field must say. There is no default row: a deficiency with no row here is a registry defect and refuses. Nothing in this registry changes DeficiencyV2, NativeCause, UnresolvedEdgeKindV1, ClosedWorldV2, the public DomainDetailCode registry or any D9 class, code or exit; every carrier it names already exists and is already closed.
x-opensip-deficiency-cause-registry.whyItIsNeeded: native-evidence section 10 labels its second column `Cause (nativeCause)` and then fills three of its rows with values that are not NativeCause members: `the unresolved edge classes; partial/not-attempted stage` for `resolution-incomplete`, `exports-open, exports-unknown` for `external-consumers-unknown`, and `compiler-inferred present` for `derivation-policy-unmet`. Each refuses schema validation as a nativeCause (`'computed-member-access' is not valid under any of the given schemas`), so the only representable value was null - which the NativeCause description itself defines as `a disclosure was owed and not made`. Worse, nothing compared the pair to anything: on the frozen reference a `resolution-incomplete` entry carrying the unrelated but schema-valid `lockfile-missing`, or relabelled `capability-missing`, or a `derivation-policy-unmet` with an empty derivationKinds, or an `external-consumers-unknown` over `exportsClosed: closed`, each closed a Run. A cause vocabulary that nothing derives and nothing compares leaves the disclosure optional in practice - the same argument that added the three body-language-* members, carried through to the rest of the table.
x-opensip-deficiency-cause-registry.whyNotMoreEnumMembers: Adding NativeCause members was rejected on the merits, not for compatibility. `resolution-incomplete` has a genuinely SET-VALUED cause: an entry can exhibit up to all sixteen UnresolvedEdgeKindV1 classes at once, and a scalar cannot carry them, so enum members would either lose information or force an arbitrary pick - the multi-cause defect the finding names. All three rows already have closed, structured, independently DERIVED carriers in the same record: unresolvedEdgeClasses (which RC-2 already forces to equal the admitted unresolved-edge facts), ClosedWorldV2.exportsClosed, and derivationKinds. The correction is to NAME those carriers and ENFORCE the join, not to duplicate them in a scalar.
x-opensip-deficiency-cause-registry.nullIsNotAnEscape: Where a row says nativeCause MUST be null, that null no longer records an unmade disclosure: the row names the field that carries the cause instead, and admission REFUSES unless that field actually carries it. A `resolution-incomplete` entry whose resolutionCompleteness claims `complete` is refused, so `null` cannot be used to say nothing.
x-opensip-deficiency-cause-registry.multiCauseAndPrecedence: An entry carries ONE deficiency and simultaneously carries every carrier this registry names. What each carrier RETAINS differs, and an earlier revision wrongly generalised the strongest case to all of them by saying the scalar `loses nothing`. The accurate statement is per carrier: resolutionCompleteness.unresolvedEdgeClasses is a genuine SET and retains EVERY applicable unresolved class at once, already forced by RC-2 to equal the admitted unresolved-edge facts of the view; closedWorld and derivationKinds are independent fields that retain their own state whatever the deficiency is; but input-closure-incomplete's carrier is a SINGLE SCALAR NativeCause, and a Run can genuinely be missing several inputs at once - two absent crates, or an absent crate AND an unavailable generated file. For that row the retained cause is a SELECTED one, not the full set. See selectedScalarCauseLimitation. Which single deficiency is declared when several apply is the section 10 precedence order, applied by the owning sufficiency evaluation against a REQUIREMENT. That selection is deliberately NOT re-derived from the entry alone, and the limit is stated rather than worked around: several conditions are requirement-relative (external-consumer state matters only for a universal negative about an exported target; the confidence floor lives in the Requirement, not the entry), and RC-3 makes `coverage: complete` with `state: incomplete` and NO deficiency a valid honest entry. Forcing a deficiency from exhibited entry evidence would therefore refuse lawful Runs. What IS decidable from the entry is the direction enforced here: a DECLARED deficiency must be SUPPORTED by the entry's own committed evidence.
x-opensip-deficiency-cause-registry.retainedVersusPublicRoute: Two different routes and neither substitutes for the other. RETAINED: the whole ViewEntryV3 lives inside the coverage2 record, whose payload digest and schema digest the Run commits, so every carrier named below is retained evidence a verifier can re-derive. PUBLIC: the DEFICIENCY is projected outward as its own closed DomainDetailCode - `resolution-incomplete`, `external-consumers-unknown` and `derivation-policy-unmet` are all already members - and the CAUSE travels as typed detail in the coverage2 record the host termination names by its coverageId, exactly as section 10 has always said for the nativeCause-carried rows. No new public code is added and none is needed.

language-tier-unsupported.rule: The admitted universe's selected grammars do not bear the requested relation@rung. The cause is a single named state, so nativeCause carries it and must be exactly capability-missing. Already derived and enforced by the syntax capability prerequisite; stated here so one table covers every member.

provider-unavailable.rule: Section 10 leaves this row's Cause cell empty, so a null is lawful and self-describing; where a more specific named state applies it is carried. No other cause may appear.

input-closure-incomplete.rule: The one deficiency whose cause genuinely IS a single named missing input, which is why section 10 lists twelve of them and why the three body-language-* members were added here. A null refuses: this row is exactly where a null would record an unmade disclosure.

budget-exhausted.rule: Section 10 already qualifies this row `(stage terminal)`. The stage terminal is the cause and it is a closed StageTerminal value in the same entry, so nativeCause is null by design and the terminal must actually say budget-exhausted.

confidence-floor-unmet.rule: Requirement-relative and deliberately without an entry carrier: the FLOOR lives in RequirementV2.minConfidenceMillionths and the entry carries only its own confidenceMillionths, so the entry cannot decide whether the floor was met. The comparison is the sufficiency evaluation's, and stating that limit is honest where inventing an entry-level predicate would not be.

derivation-policy-unmet.relationLaw: The OWNING law scopes this deficiency to one relation. Native section 4.7 and sufficiency_v2 apply derivationPolicy only where `rel == "types"` and the requirement asks for `declared-only`; there is no derivation policy for any other relation, so no other relation's entry can be short of one. An earlier revision checked the derivationKinds carrier ALONE, and a complete Run therefore admitted this declared deficiency on a `references` entry that merely carried the same array value (root diagnostic: references ADMIT, types ADMIT). An entry whose relation is outside this list cannot declare it.
derivation-policy-unmet.rule: Section 10's Cause cell reads `compiler-inferred present`, which is a statement about derivationKinds - a closed three-member set in this same entry - and not a NativeCause. The entry must actually carry compiler-inferred among its derivation kinds.
derivation-policy-unmet.thisIsDeclarationSupportNotAnObligation: Two different assertions, and only the first is enforced. (1) An entry that DECLARES this deficiency must be for relation `types` and must actually carry `compiler-inferred`. (2) Whether a given requirement DEMANDS the deficiency is sufficiency_v2's question against a RequirementV2, and is not derived here. `compiler-inferred` types are exact under the admitted universe and are perfectly valid under `derivationPolicy=any`; they become a deficiency only under `declared-only`. Nothing here imposes declared-only on a valid types entry, and controls hold both directions.

resolution-incomplete.rule: Section 10's Cause cell reads `the unresolved edge classes; partial/not-attempted stage`, and both halves are ResolutionCompletenessV2 fields: `state` names the stage condition and `unresolvedEdgeClasses` carries EVERY applicable class at once, already forced by RC-2 to equal the admitted unresolved-edge facts of this view. A claim of this deficiency over a `complete` or `not-applicable` resolution state is refused: that is the entry contradicting its own evidence.

external-consumers-unknown.rule: Section 10's Cause cell reads `exports-open, exports-unknown`, which are the ClosedWorldV2 exportsClosed values `open` and `unknown` in this same entry, not NativeCause members. `closed` refuses: an entry cannot claim its consumers are unknown while its own closed-world record says they are closed.

required-relation-missing.rule: A sufficiency verdict about a relation the view does NOT carry an entry for, so an entry can never be its own evidence. It has no entry carrier by construction and takes no cause. Kept admissible rather than refused because nothing in this contract states that a host may not record it, and inventing that refusal is not this correction's to make.

x-opensip-deficiency-cause-registry.noDeficiencyNoCause: A null deficiency requires a null nativeCause. A cause without a deficiency names why nothing went wrong, which is not a claim this record can carry.
x-opensip-deficiency-cause-registry.enforcedAt: native_evidence_model admit_coverage_result_v3 - the producer boundary - and therefore again at identity-model.v3.open_run_closure, which re-runs that exact admission over the RETAINED coverage payload (native owner admission, not evaluator correctness). identity-model.v3.close_run is complete replay of evaluator3 output. Refusals are native.coverage-cause-* and are PROVIDER.PROTOCOL_VIOLATION like the other producer-boundary refusals.
x-opensip-deficiency-cause-registry.selectedScalarCauseLimitation: STATED LIMITATION, not a defect to be engineered around. input-closure-incomplete retains ONE NativeCause while several missing inputs may coexist. Provenance of the selection: the producer names the cause it acted on, and Run closure checks that the named cause is lawful for the deficiency - it does not and cannot enumerate the inputs that were not named. What IS fully retained beside it is the rest of the Coverage entry and the Run's own evidence: the missing dependency sources, prepared rows and generated files are retained records in their own right, so a consumer that needs the complete set reads those rather than the scalar. No multi-cause format is introduced merely to make the prose true; the bounded source/ownership laws stay exactly as they are, and the limitation is published so no consumer reads the scalar as exhaustive.

perRequirementConsumerBoundary.standing: Normative and CLOSED. WHERE a per-requirement sufficiency_v2 outcome travels once it leaves this unit, and in WHICH vocabulary. This block adds no member to DeficiencyV2, changes no carrier row above, adds no D9 class, code, exit or public detail code, and changes no D9 projection: it names the consumer boundary that was previously unnamed.
perRequirementConsumerBoundary.producer: native-evidence.md section 4.6 `sufficiency_v2`, evaluated once per RequirementV2 against one NATIVE view, and therefore defined for the thirteen native fact relations only. Its FULL result is {satisfied, deficiency?, disclosures, causes}: `causes` is returned on BOTH branches - empty when satisfied - and `disclosures` may be non-empty on the FAILING branch as well. An earlier revision called the result shape closed and total as {satisfied:true,disclosures} or {satisfied:false,deficiency}; that described only the two fields a consumer projects, not the producer's output, and is corrected here.

consumers.carries: the DeficiencyV2 member sufficiency_v2 returned for THIS requirement
consumers.vocabulary: urn:opensip:product-v1:workflows:common#/$defs/NativeSufficiencyDeficiency for a NATIVE-plane requirement - a generated/drift-checked mirror of #/$defs/DeficiencyV2 in its declared member order, because the workflows bundle resolves only workflows URNs and takes no cross-bundle $ref. An IMPORTED-plane requirement of the same record carries #/$defs/ImportedRequirementDeficiency instead, under its own owning law; the field admits either vocabulary and the boundary decides which one this relation may use.
consumers.presenceLaw: REQUIRED exactly when satisfied is false; FORBIDDEN when satisfied is true; `satisfied` must be an actual boolean; and an explicit null is refused in BOTH branches, because a present key with a null value is not an absent key. Schema-enforced in repair.schema.json and decided again by workflows_model.admit_evidence_requirement, which routes every violation to CONFIG.INVALID - the class the owning schema validation and admit_atom already use for a malformed input - and adds no public detail code. The two boundaries are held EQUAL on an enumerated shape table, except for the cross-plane rows: this schema deliberately leaves the authoritative relation-registry lookup to admission. Its oneOf admits either outcome vocabulary on either relation; admission decides the plane from registry membership. JSON Schema can branch on const/enum under a broader string type, but this schema does not duplicate that registry as conditionals or fetch its rows. This is the selected division between schema validation and admission, not a limitation caused by the relation type.
consumers.authorityLimit: The field is a DISCLOSURE, not a grant and not a gate input. `applicable` is false whenever any requirement is unsatisfied, the evidence authority stays the sealed Run named by evidenceRunId, and apply requires a security authorization bound to the exact repairPlanId - which every edit to this value changes.

perRequirementConsumerBoundary.whyNotTheD9Vocabulary: The field previously named workflows common#/$defs/D9Deficiency, which cannot express four of the nine members its only producer emits: derivation-policy-unmet, external-consumers-unknown, input-closure-incomplete and resolution-incomplete have no member there. Only three readings were conforming and no document chose between them: write the D9-mapped value, which is `verdict-indeterminate` for ALL FOUR and therefore collapses exactly the per-row distinction this registry exists to keep - including resolution-incomplete, which section 4.6 step 6 mandates for a universal negative under unresolvedEdgePolicy=forbid over an affected target and which is the outcome a destructive unused-code repair recipe turns on; write the sufficiency value and be schema-invalid for four of nine; or omit the optional field and drop the disclosure. The repair is to retype the ONE per-requirement field, not to widen D9Deficiency: that enum is the whole-Run and comparison-step termination vocabulary of the inherited D9 exit contract, three of its members (convergence-exhausted, baseline-recipe-unsupported, query-completeness-unmet) name outcomes no per-requirement evaluation can produce, and widening it would change a D9 vocabulary to fix a workflows record. The DomainDetailCode route does not resolve it either: that registry carries a DIFFERENT five of the nine (budget-exhausted plus the four above), so the union of the two covers all nine and neither single field does.

threeDistinctThingsNotToConflate.nativeOutcome: the DeficiencyV2 member for one requirement - what this block routes.
threeDistinctThingsNotToConflate.publicD9Termination: the class/exit/errorCode of the Run or step that carries the requirement - unchanged, still the section 10 table columns (indeterminate (3) with VERDICT.INDETERMINATE, COVERAGE.PROVIDER_UNAVAILABLE or COVERAGE.BUDGET_EXHAUSTED) and still spelled with D9Deficiency where a D9 record needs a deficiency.
threeDistinctThingsNotToConflate.retainedCause: the Coverage entry's own cause carrier - entry.nativeCause or the named structured field per the `deficiencies` rows above. The requirement record carries the OUTCOME and never the carrier: several outcomes are requirement-relative (the confidence floor lives in RequirementV2; external-consumer state matters only for a universal negative about an exported target) and required-relation-missing has no entry at all, so a carrier could not be copied here even in principle.
threeDistinctThingsNotToConflate.satisfiedState: a boolean about THIS requirement, not a verdict and not a coverage state. satisfied=true may still carry section 4.6 disclosures, which are not deficiencies and are not carried by this field.

perRequirementConsumerBoundary.enforcedAt: workflows_model.admit_evidence_requirement (the repair-preview producer/consumer boundary, run before any descriptor exists, refusals native.sufficiency-outcome-* under CONFIG.INVALID), the repair.schema.json presence law, and the cross-unit parity and plane-routing controls in docs/coop/design-corrections/check-integration.py.
perRequirementConsumerBoundary.driftIsAFailureNotAWidening: A member added to or removed from DeficiencyV2 without the same change in the workflows mirror fails the cross-unit parity control. The mirror is never allowed to be a superset: a workflows record must not be able to state a native outcome this unit does not define.
perRequirementConsumerBoundary.whatTheConsumerCarries: the SATISFACTION/DEFICIENCY PROJECTION of that result: `satisfied`, and exactly one DeficiencyV2 member when it is false, chosen by the section 10 precedence. `causes` and `disclosures` are NOT projected. They are the PRODUCER RESULT ARRAYS of that evaluation and are not fields of any record here: they are not members of CoverageResultV3, and some of them could not be - the confidence floor lives in RequirementV2, the external-consumer condition is requirement-relative, and `required-relation-missing` has no Coverage entry at all. What IS retained, and what a verifier re-derives, is the evidence the evaluation READ: the `coverage2` record with its own deficiency and nativeCause carrier per section 10, and the rest of the Run's committed closure. So the accurate statement is that the projection drops nothing that was retained, and that re-deriving the full result means re-running the evaluation over that retained evidence - not reading `causes` out of a stored field. No new wire field is introduced to carry them. The projection is total in the only sense a consumer needs: a failing requirement always has exactly one reported outcome, so omitting it is never lawful.
perRequirementConsumerBoundary.thisBlockOwnsTheNativePlaneOnly: Repair also admits a requirement over the two IMPORTED-EVIDENCE relations, `runtime-observation` and `history-change`. They mint no fact2, carry no sourceUniverse/targetUniverse and have no Coverage entry, so sufficiency_v2 has nothing to range over and would only report `required-relation-missing`, which says nothing true about an import. Their outcomes are owned by workflows/schemas/imported-evidence.schema.json#/x-opensip-imported-requirement-law and carry a DISJOINT vocabulary. An earlier revision described sufficiency_v2 as the only defined producer of that consumer field; that was false for those two relations and is corrected here. Which plane applies is decided at ADMISSION from relation-registry membership, never from the value.

x-opensip-config-node-kind-law.standing: Normative and CLOSED. THE authority for TypeScriptConfigGraphV1 node `kind`. The schema enum publishes the three admissible values; this law publishes which one each node's path takes, which the prose previously delegated to `the schema and native admission` while neither stated it. It adds no enum member, no field and no record.
x-opensip-config-node-kind-law.appliesTo: EVERY node of the retained graph - the selected entry AND every non-entry node reached through `extendsResolved`. There is no entry-only rule and no default for the rest. A non-entry node's kind affects no derived value (see derivedValueScope), which is exactly WHY it needed a published rule: nothing else pins it and it is still committed to the identity.
x-opensip-config-node-kind-law.rule: kind is a total function of `node.path` alone. Take the BASENAME - the final `/`-separated segment of the path - and compare it BYTE-EXACTLY against the closed table below. A match takes the table's value; anything else is `other`. Nothing else is consulted: not the file's content, not its position in the graph, not whether it is the entry, not the directory, and not any caller assertion.
x-opensip-config-node-kind-law.comparison: EXACT and case-SENSITIVE over the whole basename, on the UTF-8 bytes of the CanonicalPath as retained. No prefix, suffix, glob or stem matching; no case folding; no Unicode normalization beyond what CanonicalPath already requires; no extension-only test. `TSConfig.json`, `.tsconfig.json` and `tsconfig.jsonc` are each `other`, and a host that lowercases the basename on a case-insensitive filesystem before comparing has produced a different graph and a different identity.

examples.note: a jsconfig entry stays a jsconfig program even when its bases are not
NON-ENTRY, reached as a base: the basename decides, the depth does not
THE DISCRIMINATING CASE. The widespread tsconfig*.json convention is NOT the rule here; see whyExactAndNotThePrefixConvention
same, as a shared base of the entry
case variant: the comparison is case-sensitive
an explicitly selected custom-named TypeScript configuration; its ENTRY kind is other and it still derives configOrigin tsconfig

x-opensip-config-node-kind-law.derivedValueScope: `configOrigin` is derived from the SELECTED ENTRY node's kind only: `jsconfig` for a jsconfig entry, otherwise `tsconfig`, and `synthesized` exactly when there is no entry. So `other` and `tsconfig` both derive `tsconfig` at the entry, and a non-entry node's kind derives nothing at all. That is the whole reason this law is owed: `configOrigin` does NOT pin `kind`, so without a published rule two conforming hosts could disagree on a value that no derived field would ever contradict.
x-opensip-config-node-kind-law.identityConsequence: kind sits INSIDE the hashed record. `tsconfigGraphHash` is the raw SHA-256 of C(TypeScriptConfigGraphV1); TypeScriptUniverseV2ResolvedInputs REQUIRES it and the binding checks equality; the universe H identity is fact.sourceUniverse and subject-scope.sourceUniverse, hence fact2, scope2, coverage2, view2, evidence3, seal3 and run3. Native owner admission re-runs this over retained payloads at identity-model.v3.open_run_closure; complete replay is identity-model.v3.close_run. Two readings of one repository containing `tsconfig.build.json` would therefore mint two RunIds and defeat independent replay across machines - the same defect class the analysis-spec `capabilityId` vocabulary was closed for, and closed the same way: by naming the authority beside the field. The historical evaluator2 graph reached evidence2/seal2/run2; that is the historical counterexample, not a current qualified claim.
x-opensip-config-node-kind-law.whyExactAndNotThePrefixConvention: Both readings are natural and they disagree on real files, so one had to be chosen and written down. Exact basenames are chosen because `kind` records WHICH RECOGNIZED CONFIGURATION FILE this node is, not what a project chose to name a base; because the exact table is TOTAL, decidable from the retained path alone and identical on every filesystem, whereas a prefix rule would additionally have to decide `jsconfig.build.json`, an extensionless `tsconfig` and `tsconfig.jsonc`; and because it is the rule the selected model already derives, so publishing it changes no existing value. `other` is not a defect classification: it is the honest statement that this node's basename is neither recognized name, which is exactly what an explicitly selected custom-named configuration presents. NOTE ON SCOPE: this rationale is internal to this design. No claim is made here about what any external toolchain recognizes or what meaning it assigns to a filename convention; such a claim would be unverified from these bytes and is not needed to fix the reading.

x-opensip-public-route-registry.originatingBoundaryLaw: admission-and-qualification section 1 fixes the actor/layer split: `Invalid external input is an admission rejection with the existing carrier's D9 code; an invalid host-generated internal layer is a host invariant fault.` The inherited d9-exit-contract.v1.14 completes it: nonAnalysisDerivation rule 2 puts authored-config errors and failed preconditions in request-rejected, rule 5 puts HOST failures in operational-failed, and axes.domainCondition distinguishes `host-fault` from `precondition-failed`. x-opensip-public-route-registry.helperDoesNotGuessOrigin: The pure admission helpers - admit_requested_capabilities, admit_release_capability_registry, deficiency_cause_faults - are passed rows and nothing about provenance, so they emit the internal decision key ALONE. public_termination_for(key, origin) is the derivation the HOST calls with the origin it already holds; it refuses an origin the key cannot have, so a caller cannot launder a configuration error into a host fault or the reverse.
x-opensip-public-route-registry.hostInvariantSuccessor: SELECTED NORMATIVE D9 COMPOSITION, published here rather than deferred. It inherits docs/coop/artifacts/d9-exit-contract.v1.14.json UNCHANGED and adds exactly one thing: the faultCause `host-invariant`, mapped to the EXISTING error code SYSTEM.OUTCOME.ILLEGAL_STATE. What was unrepresentable was the host-INVARIANT subtype specifically - other host-fault causes such as host-io, ledger-corrupt and provider-protocol already existed and were always representable - because StepTermination requires operational-failed to carry BOTH an errorCode and a non-none faultCause, and no declared cause named a host invariant violation. Borrowing host-io for it would be a different remedy. PRECISION: codeMaps.rule's `total and injective` is a property of the DECLARED CAUSE DOMAIN - every declared cause has exactly one code - and does NOT require every errorCode to have a preimage, so an errorCode without a cause was not a violation of totality; the earlier claim that the maps were non-total was wrong. Existing classes, exit codes, reason codes and error codes are unchanged, but this IS a D9 vocabulary extension: faultCause grows by one member, and saying otherwise would be false. Schema, workflow mapper and this registry must agree, every inherited mapping and golden is preserved, and an unknown cause still refuses.

The tuple names one cell of work for one unit and `required` is its attribute. Distinct rows can disagree on requiredness, whose value decides whether a missing Coverage entry contributes indeterminate; if admitted, that contradiction would enter analysisSpecDigest and PlanId. Default construction can instead produce identical rows through a host invariant violation. Both cases violate the one-row-per-tuple law; the precise admission paths are stated below. x-opensip-public-route-registry.aliasMapIsContextFree: Only a key whose public DETAIL is the same for EVERY origin may appear in public-detail-registry internalAliases, because that map is context-free. Two keys qualify and are aliased there: native.requested-capability-mode-not-selected -> PROVIDER.NOT_SELECTED and native.release-capability-undeclared -> native.capability-unavailable. The origin-DEPENDENT keys deliberately are NOT in that map - a context-free alias cannot express `CONFIG.INVALID when configured, absent when the host produced it` - and the keys whose detail is absent need no alias because they never surface as a DomainDetailCode. An earlier revision claimed all 14 belonged there and that the edit was mechanical; both claims were wrong.
x-opensip-public-route-registry.enforcedAt: native_evidence_model public_termination_for derives the termination and validates it against the real StepTermination schema; the guards themselves emit only the internal key.
x-opensip-public-route-registry.possibleOriginsLaw: Every key declares the boundaries at which it CAN arise, and a derivation refuses any other. A release declaration is never a user's configuration and a configured capability is never the host's own authenticated release input, so a caller cannot launder one actor's fault into another's. An origin-INDEPENDENT key still has possible origins - what is independent is the resulting class and code, not who could have caused it.
x-opensip-public-route-registry.unsupportedTypedIsNotOnThisTable: An UNSUPPORTED-TYPED request is admitted and ANSWERED, never refused: the Run closes and its Coverage carries `unknown` with the deficiency the OWNING DERIVATION selects under the section 10 precedence. For a relation the admitted universe cannot serve at all - a compiler-free references request under syntax-only - that is language-tier-unsupported with capability-missing, and it OUTRANKS provider-unavailable. A capability the release merely did not declare available carries provider-unavailable with capability-missing only where no more specific deficiency applies, and a CANDIDATE-ONLY capability has no Coverage entry at all - its public route is the advisory native.capability-unavailable notice in CommandEnvelope.availability, whose complete ownership tuple is defined in section 1.4. An earlier revision stated the provider-unavailable pair here as THE outcome for both cases, which contradicted the precedence and the candidate-only distinction section 1.4 publishes. Neither case may be converted into an admission refusal.
x-opensip-public-route-registry.envelopeErrorsComposition: A kind=failure CommandEnvelope REQUIRES a nonempty `errors` array of DomainDetail, so `termination.domainDetail` being OPTIONAL does not complete the public failure surface: a route that lawfully leaves it absent still owes the envelope a detail. An earlier revision stopped at StepTermination admission, and a minimal failure envelope built from the externally-supplied and host-generated routes refused `errors is a required property`. failure_envelope_errors composes it: where the termination carries a detail the array is EXACTLY that detail, so the two surfaces can never disagree; where it does not, the route's own `envelopeDetail` supplies one. Every code used is a member of the closed public DomainDetailCode registry. Four members were ADDED there rather than borrowing an unrelated remedy - native.capability-spec-invalid, native.release-declaration-invalid, native.coverage-cause-unsupported and HOST.INVARIANT_VIOLATED - because `a supplied spec names an unregistered capability`, `the installed release declaration is malformed`, `the provider emitted an unsupported deficiency/cause pair` and `the host violated its own invariant` are four different things for a caller to do next. Reuse was taken wherever it was honest: external configuration keeps CONFIG.INVALID and a NOT-SELECTED cell keeps PROVIDER.NOT_SELECTED. Before a Plan or Run exists no run envelope is fabricated - the failure envelope carries the termination, its errors and the request id, and nothing else.
x-opensip-public-route-registry.remedyKeyingConstraint: NORMATIVE MAINTENANCE CONSTRAINT on the remedy table, promoted here from a source comment so it is part of the published law rather than advice a reader may miss. PUBLIC_ROUTE_REMEDIES is keyed by PUBLIC CODE, not by internal key. Several keys route to one code - native.requested-capability-unregistered, native.requested-capability-mode-unregistered and native.requested-capability-duplicate-ownership-tuple all reach CONFIG.INVALID under external-configuration, and all three reach native.capability-spec-invalid as the externally-supplied-spec envelope detail - so ONE string must remain true for EVERY key that reaches that code, and a key whose remedy would be a DIFFERENT next step may not simply reuse the code. THIS IS CURRENTLY SATISFIED, not merely intended: the two strings widened for the ownership tuple state both the unregistered-name condition and the one-row-per-tuple condition, and the default-construction path added later routes to the same key and is covered by the same two sentences plus HOST.INVARIANT_VIOLATED, which is true of a host emitting two rows for one cell. The structural alternative - keying the remedy by (code, internal key) - is deliberately NOT taken: it changes the shape of an existing table for a case honest sentences already cover, and no key in this composition needs it. What is owed instead is exact: adding a key that routes to an existing code obliges its author to check that code's remedy is a true next step for the new condition and to widen it or choose another code if it is not.
x-opensip-public-route-registry.subjectNormalization: The guards emit COLON-SUFFIXED refusal strings - native.requested-capability-unregistered:made-up-capability, native.coverage-cause-not-for-deficiency:input-closure-incomplete:capability-missing - so a normalizer matching the whole string would find no registered key. normalize_internal_key matches the LONGEST registered key followed by a colon and takes the remainder as the subject, which is what reaches DomainDetail.subject so a caller sees WHICH value was refused. A raw string matching no registered key REFUSES (native.public-route-key-unregistered) rather than passing through, as the public registry aliasRule requires of an unknown key; an origin a key cannot have refuses too (native.public-route-origin-not-possible).
x-opensip-public-route-registry.subjectBoundLaw: DomainDetail.subject is BoundedText (1024) while a refused VALUE can be far longer: a structurally valid languageMode may be 4096 characters, and the composed subject then reached 4149 and made the whole failure envelope schema-invalid at termination.domainDetail.subject or errors[0].subject. bounded_subject elides: the registered KEY is preserved verbatim - it selects the code, the class and the origin - and only the offending value is elided, keeping a leading window plus the SHA-256 of the untruncated subject's UTF-8 bytes. UNITS, because the two operations differ: `raw` is the composed subject as an admitted UNICODE SCALAR STRING, and length and slicing count UNICODE CODE POINTS - what BoundedText's JSON Schema maxLength counts - not UTF-8 bytes and not UTF-16 code units; the SHA-256 input is exactly raw encoded as UTF-8 with NO additional normalization, rendered as 64 lowercase hex characters after the ASCII marker `...#sha256:`, giving exactly 1024 code points. A non-ASCII value can therefore have a UTF-8 byte length above 1024 while its scalar length does not, and the two must not be conflated. GUARANTEE: distinct long values are distinguished under the ORDINARY COLLISION-RESISTANCE ASSUMPTION for SHA-256, not by any impossibility claim, and the guarantee is confined to what is PUBLISHED - the bounded subject and its digest. No separate retained store of the untruncated value is promised or named here; a host keeping its own operational log matches it by recomputing this digest. Emitting the untruncated string would be schema-invalid, dropping the subject would lose attribution, and reclassifying the input error as success would be false; the code, class and origin are never changed by the elision.

x-opensip-grammar-capability-registry.standing: Normative and CLOSED. The per-language capability mapping of the bundled grammar set, published here so a consumer can reconstruct it without reading author code. syntaxClass is NOT caller-selected: a grammar row declaring a class other than the one this registry assigns to its languageId is refused at grammar-bundle admission, in both directions.
x-opensip-grammar-capability-registry.source: native_evidence_model.v2.BUNDLED_GRAMMARS (the same table the shared discovery rule uses for the grammar-only membership path) and native-evidence section 6.3.

classLaw.code: The language has the section 6.3 body spans - function, method, closure/lambda, impl item and block bodies - and a published L2/L3 normalisation table. Bears clone body identity (clones@normalized-body-hash) and the code-construct syntax relations (declares/literal/control-flow @ syntactic). Its languageId MUST be a member of foundation body-language-version.languageId, because that identifier enters the clone preimage.
classLaw.data-document: A bundled grammar for a data or document format. It has no section 6.3 body spans, and this kit publishes no tokenisation, literalKind mapping or normalisation law for it. Its files are grammar-only MEMBERS - accounted, inventoried, never unsupported-file - bearing file/package/vcs-change inventory evidence under the syntax universe. It mints NO body identity, no suffix of it appears in the syntax dialect table, and its languageId MUST NOT be in body-language-version.languageId. A clone or code-construct request against it is explicitly UNAVAILABLE (language-tier-unsupported for that capability), never a complete empty clone result, which would read as a finding of no clones.

x-opensip-grammar-capability-registry.unbundledLanguages: A language with no bundled grammar is not representable here at all: its files are unsupported-file with reason no-bundled-grammar, and its languageId is outside the SyntaxGrammarBundleV1 vocabulary. Adding one is a deliberate registry change, not a caller choice.
x-opensip-grammar-capability-registry.futureCapability: Data-format syntax facts (for example literal@syntactic over JSON or YAML) would require a published tokenisation and literalKind law. None exists in this kit, so the mapping above does not promise them. This is a bounded future capability, deliberately not invented here.
x-opensip-grammar-capability-registry.enforcementBoundaries: This registry is the authority at THREE boundaries, not one. (1) Grammar-bundle admission: a row's declared syntaxClass must equal the registered one, in both directions. (2) Every admitted fact2 under a syntax universe: every ANCHOR PATH must be read by a SELECTED grammar whose capability set contains that relation@rung. (3) Every requested subject-scope under a syntax universe, INCLUDING an empty view: judged on the committed examined extent, where a code capability needs at least one extent path read by a selected code grammar, and a capability no selected grammar bears is unavailable. INVENTORY CAPABILITIES (file@enumerated, package@manifest-declared, vcs-change@vcs-reported) are ALWAYS available and are never grammar-gated at boundary (2) OR boundary (3). An earlier revision stated that exemption only inside boundary (3), and boundary (2) read as an unconditional every-anchor rule; a literal implementer therefore refused the very inventory facts boundary (3) had just promised were unconditionally available, which made an inventoried .py path inventoriable and unrepresentable at the same time. The exemption belongs to both because it is a property of the RELATION, not of the boundary: an inventory fact is not read by a grammar at all - it is the snapshot inventory row, the manifest declaration or the VCS observation - so there is no grammar for it to be gated on. Independently of this exemption the relation registry anchorLaw closes the inventory class at ZERO anchors, so an inventory fact names no anchor path for boundary (2) to test in the first place; the two laws agree and neither depends on the other. An earlier revision enforced only (1), which constrains what a bundle says about itself and not what a Run claims: Markdown declares facts, complete empty declares/clones Coverage and references@resolved-binding under resolutionAttempted=false all admitted. None of the three consults a claimed coverage value, a caller-declared class, or whether facts exist.
x-opensip-grammar-capability-registry.unavailableRequestDisclosure: A well-formed request for a capability this universe cannot serve is DISCLOSED, not answered and not refused outright: coverage `unknown`, deficiency `language-tier-unsupported`, nativeCause `capability-missing` - existing vocabulary, mapped in native-evidence section 10. A false `complete`, a wrong or null cause and a wrong deficiency each refuse with their own typed reason. The capability is retained: a data-grammar inventory Run and a code-grammar declares/clones Run still close with a genuine complete and no deficiency.
x-opensip-grammar-capability-registry.selectionMatters: An UNSELECTED grammar lends no capability. Selection is committed in the universe identity, so a bundle that ships a grammar the universe did not select cannot make its capabilities available.
x-opensip-grammar-capability-registry.inventoryIsNotGrammarGated: Normative. A snapshot inventories every file it contains, including ones no bundled grammar reads, so requiring a grammar per inventory row would silently narrow the promise this registry makes. The three inventory capabilities are therefore exempt at every boundary this registry owns, on every path - unsupported suffix, extensionless, data-document and code alike - and a `vcs-change` on a `deleted` path that is not in the snapshot at all. This is an exemption from GRAMMAR OWNERSHIP only. It does not exempt an inventory fact from its relation's snapshot joins (path in the inventory; for `file` also the content digest, the byte length and custody of the retained bytes), from own-scope attribution, or from the anchorLaw; and it does not make a CODE fact admissible merely because some other anchor of the same Run is on a supported path.

NativeCause.description: The typed cause carried beside a DeficiencyV2 in a Coverage entry. The three body-language-* members are the clones ownership states that identity-and-evidence and native-evidence section 11 require the clones Coverage to DISCLOSE: the contract mandates that such a scope mint no body identity, that its Coverage report the incompleteness, and that the predicate and seal be indeterminate rather than a false pass -- and until these members existed no value in this closed vocabulary could name why. A nullable nativeCause does not satisfy a mandated disclosure; a null there records that a disclosure was owed and not made. The other selectionLaw causes deliberately have NO member here: BODY_LANGUAGE_OWNER_NOT_COMPILED and BODY_LANGUAGE_OWNER_NOT_SELECTED are per-body refusals that section 11 states are compatible with coverage=complete (the host examined that subject and correctly produced no fact for it), and BODY_LANGUAGE_DIALECT_ABSENT/BODY_LANGUAGE_DIALECT_AMBIGUOUS are universe-level dialect faults that refuse before any Coverage entry is minted.

capabilityId.description: A member of native/native-capability-matrix.v2.json#/capabilities[].id. The pattern is the product-configuration analysis.capabilities item pattern, which contains no `@`, so a relation@rung spelling is refused by shape before membership is even consulted. Membership itself is checked at admission: the pattern is necessary and never sufficient.

languageModes.description: The language modes this release declares the capability applicable to. Each must be a registered mode whose (capability, mode) cell is not NOT-SELECTED.

ReleaseCapabilityDeclarationV1.description: One row of the authenticated release declaration registry named by native-evidence section 1.4 and admission-and-qualification section 1.1. The CONTENT is release-specific and remains an authenticated input; this schema, the membership authority in the capability matrix capabilityIdLaw, the canonical spelling and the binding to Plan are normative.

ReleaseCapabilityRegistryV1.description: The authenticated release declaration registry as a whole. Rows are unique; a duplicate capabilityId refuses rather than being merged, because two rows declaring different applicable modes for one capability would leave default selection ambiguous.

ResolutionCompletenessState.description: Which member is legal on a given entry is decided by RC-1 (native-evidence.md section 4.3) and is NOT schema-decidable: applicability is total over the registered (relation, rung) pairs and turns on membership of the RUNG in the closed five-member resolved set (resolved-target, resolved-binding, resolved-callee, checked, from-resolved-calls), never on the relation ladder length. A resolved rung must never be not-applicable - reachability@from-resolved-calls is a one-rung relation whose single rung IS resolved - and every other registered rung, including unresolved-edge@observed and types@annotated as well as the syntactic rungs, is not-applicable with attempted=false, unresolvedEdgeCount=0 and unresolvedEdgeClasses=[]. RC-0 runs first and is relation-specific: the pair must be registered, meaning the rung is a member of THAT relation's own ladder, so unresolved-edge@enumerated is refused although both tokens are registered. That check and the not-applicable minting law (attempted false, count 0, empty class list) are enforced by coverage_bijection at the producer boundary AND again at retained Run closure, and they hold for a FACT-FREE entry over an empty examined scope. not-applicable is never a fallback for an unregistered pair. stageTerminal is deliberately not constrained: a not-applicable entry may retain the stage terminal its producer observed.

x-opensip-digest.artifact: the exact inventoried snapshot bytes of the unit marker file

WorkspaceUnitV1.description: Superseded by WorkspaceUnitV2 (per-language units may share a rootPath). Retained only so the v1 case fixtures remain readable.

coverage.description: The ANSWER over the examined partition, and the second committed encoding of the section 4.1 claim-1 question `did we look at every subject?`. RC-6, enforced by the cross-property admission check rather than encoded in this shape schema: coverage=complete REQUIRES resolutionCompleteness.examinedExhaustive=true. It is an IMPLICATION, never an equality. coverage=unknown constrains examinedExhaustive in NEITHER direction: a host may examine the committed partition exhaustively and still answer unknown because the evidence it needs is missing rather than unexamined (ambiguous or missing Rust compilation ownership, an undeclared or unservable capability, an unlisted source variant), and it may also answer unknown because the examination itself was cut short. Only the converse is impossible: complete over a partition the producer says it did not examine exhaustively asserts a totality the same record disclaims.
