Rung.description: A resolution rung NAME. This replaces the withdrawn abstract Resolution tier vocabulary (syntax/resolved/type/external), which was disjoint from the rung names every fact, Coverage entry and native RequirementV2 actually carries, had no published mapping onto them, and was compared by a single global rank table across all relations. The inherited C-1 law is that ordering is PER-RELATION and never global, so an abstract tier could only ever be a partial, lossy, relation-dependent renaming of the rung it names; the atom now names the rung directly. This enum is the flat vocabulary and is a NECESSARY condition only: it is exactly the union of the ladders in foundation/relation-payload-schemas.v2.json#/x-opensip-relation-registry (the single ladder authority) and is drift-checked against it. Membership of THIS atom's relation's ladder is the sufficient condition and is enforced at admission, because no schema keyword can express it without restating the ladders and creating another independent source.

requirement.description: required: absent/stale/unmapped evidence makes the rule indeterminate. optional: the rule evaluates without it and discloses IMPORT.ABSENT_FOR_PREDICATE.

relation.description: Either one of the thirteen native fact relations closed by foundation/relation-payload-schemas.v2.json#/x-opensip-relation-registry, or one of the imported-evidence relations closed by imported-evidence.schema.json#/x-opensip-evidence-relation-registry. Any other identifier refuses at policy admission. The identifier syntax is all a schema keyword can express here; closed membership is decided at admission against those two registries, which are the authorities.

minResolution.description: A rung of THIS atom's relation's ladder. Satisfaction is ladder-index comparison within that one relation: an admitted fact satisfies the atom when its rung's index is at least this rung's index in the same ladder. A rung of another relation is not a weaker or stronger value, it is a refusal.

evidence.description: for atoms over imported evidence subjects (e.g. relation runtime-observation); the rule must declare a matching evidenceUse

gate.description: true: a finding of this rule fails the verdict when live and unwaived; false: advisory

emitWhen.description: a finding is emitted for a subject when this predicate is TRUE; FALSE is a retained no-match; INDETERMINATE is a typed deficiency for the rule

expires.description: null: no expiry. Expiry is resolved at Plan construction against the admitted trust clock; expired waivers are removed from the effective set and disclosed as POLICY.WAIVER_EXPIRED. Two waivers with an equal target are POLICY.DUPLICATE_WAIVER (request-rejected).

waivers.description: sorted ascending by waiverId; waiverId unique

WaiverResolutionV1.description: Disclosure emitted at Plan construction; operational, not identity-bearing (the resolved effective set's digest is).

rules.description: ruleId unique; sorted ascending by ruleId UTF-8 bytes

emitWhen.description: a finding is emitted for a subject when this predicate is TRUE; FALSE is a retained no-match; INDETERMINATE is a typed deficiency for the rule

AtomSuccessorV1.description: Proposed Atom extension: optional endpoint. Root integrates into policy-document.schema.json. Default source when omitted.

value.x-opensip-profile-major-law: PolicyDocumentV2 is explicitly schemaMajor2, RuleProgramV2 schemaVersion2. WaiverSetV1 and ScopeDocumentV1 retain their old owner document and bytes. Policy1 is not silently relabelled or evaluated as policy2.

value.title: Imported evidence: one foundation import2 wrapper, typed payloads as content (PROPOSED, revised)
value.description: Import is an operational admission step (import custody), never an analysis Run. There is exactly ONE import identity: importId = H('import', foundation import descriptor) from foundation/identity-schemas.v2.json#/$defs/import (schemaVersion 2). The typed payload records here (runtime, test, history) and native's typed records (dependency-source, prepared-output, and native's runtime-coverage/test-results/history payload grammars) are PAYLOADS: their bytes are referenced by payloadDigest (raw SHA-256 of the canonical payload bytes) and their registered schema by payloadSchemaDigest. The wrapper's identity therefore differs from the payload content hash, and one payload can appear under two wrappers only if correspondence/producer/adapter/scope also agree, which is the intended meaning. Hostile-input bounds: artifact at most 268435456 bytes; at most 1048576 subjects; at most 4096 blobs; JSON depth at most 32; strict UTF-8, no duplicate keys, no float lexemes, no surrogates. Observed no-hits during one window are never universal non-use; only observable-unhit subjects may be consumed by a predicate, and only with the window/population disclosed.

x-opensip-evidence-relation-registry.standing: Normative and closed. A policy atom may name a relation from exactly two places: the thirteen NATIVE fact relations closed by foundation/relation-payload-schemas.v2.json#/x-opensip-relation-registry, or the imported-evidence relations below. An atom naming anything else refuses at policy admission; there is no open relation namespace and no default.
x-opensip-evidence-relation-registry.why: Atoms range over imported-evidence subjects as well as native facts, and the same per-relation ladder law must decide their minResolution. Without a ladder for these relations the atom's rung is undecidable, which is the other half of the withdrawn abstract-tier vocabulary. These relations are deliberately NOT added to the native fact registry: they mint no fact2, they carry no sourceUniverse/targetUniverse, and that registry stays closed at thirteen.
x-opensip-evidence-relation-registry.ladderRule: Same law as native relations: the ladder is that relation's own total order, weakest-first, and minResolution must be a member of it. Nothing orders a rung of one relation against a rung of another.
x-opensip-evidence-relation-registry.rungVocabulary: No new rung token is introduced. `observed` is already the registered rung of the native `unresolved-edge` relation, and an import carries exactly one strength of claim: the observation was made. Window, population, observability and completeness are carried by the payload and the closed-world machinery, never by the rung.
x-opensip-evidence-relation-registry.evidenceDeclarationRule: An atom naming one of these relations MUST carry `evidence` equal to that relation's evidenceKind, and its rule must declare a matching evidenceUse. An atom naming a native fact relation MUST NOT carry `evidence`. This keeps the two planes separable at admission rather than by convention.

PayloadBinding.description: Closed table row: which registered payload schema each import kind admits and which contract owns the payload semantics.

payloadDomain.description: ONE registry, five rows: runtime/test/history admit ONLY the workflow payload domains (native's runtime-coverage/test-results/history adapter grammars are normalized by native into these payloads BEFORE import and are not import payload domains); dependency/prepared admit ONLY native.import-payload.dependency-source.v1 / native.import-payload.prepared-output.v1 (native-evidence.md §7 spellings).

schemaDocument.description: the registered schema DOCUMENT whose exact complete bytes hash to payloadSchemaDigest (raw SHA-256 of the file bytes; no canonical-schema hash exists)

selector.description: JSON pointer of the payload $def inside schemaDocument; the selector identifies the definition, the digest binds the document bytes

PayloadRegistryV1.description: The one closed import payload registry. Exactly these five rows exist; any other (kind, payloadDomain) pair is IMPORT.KIND_PAYLOAD_MISMATCH and a domain with no row is IMPORT.PAYLOAD_SCHEMA_UNREGISTERED.

SourceMappingV1.description: The one closed mapping artifact that makes vcs-revision/declared-build evidence consumable. Producing recipe: the adapter that generated the runtime/test artifact emits, for every generated path it observed, the digest of the generated bytes and the digest and path of the snapshot source it was built from; the host admits the mapping only when every sourceSha256 equals the snapshot2 inventory digest of sourcePath (else IMPORT.SOURCE_MAPPING_REQUIRED and the evidence stays unmapped-only). Digest: raw SHA-256 of the canonical bytes, retained as a blob and carried in SourceCorrespondence.sourceMappingDigest.

entries.description: sorted ascending by generatedPath; generatedPath unique

ImportScopeDescriptor.description: Exact mirror of foundation identity-schemas.v2.json#/$defs/scope-descriptor: the foundation record is the AUTHORITY and this document restates it field-for-field, including every array's owning x-opensip-order. wrapper.scopeDigest = raw SHA-256 of the canonical bytes of this record (the same producing rule as plan.scopeDigest); retained as a blob. There is no separate workflow import-scope domain. Because one digest preimage is admitted through both documents, they must admit and refuse exactly the same bytes; the mirror-drift check proves it rather than asserting it.

ImportObservationV1.description: Closed preimage of wrapper.observationDigest (raw SHA-256 of canonical bytes; retained blob). Null members mean the observation semantics do not apply to the kind.

BuildIdentityV1.description: Closed preimage of wrapper.buildDigest (raw SHA-256 of canonical bytes; retained blob).

ImportWrapperV2.description: Exact mirror of foundation import descriptor fields (schemaVersion 2). Every auxiliary digest is a raw SHA-256 of the canonical bytes of an exact closed record retained as a blob (identity-and-evidence §2 auxiliary-digest rule); none is an H(domain) identity: payloadSchemaDigest = raw SHA-256 of the exact registered schema DOCUMENT bytes (PayloadRegistryV1 row); payloadDigest = raw SHA-256 of the canonical payload bytes; sourceCorrespondenceDigest = raw SHA-256 of canonical common#SourceCorrespondence; buildDigest = raw SHA-256 of canonical BuildIdentityV1; scopeDigest = raw SHA-256 of canonical ImportScopeDescriptor (= foundation scope-descriptor); observationDigest = raw SHA-256 of canonical ImportObservationV1. importId = 'import2:' + H('import', this object) is the only H-domain identity in an import. No hidden metadata: every field is one of these thirteen.

ImportedEvidenceRecordV1.description: Operational custody record joining the wrapper, its payload binding, the resolved correspondence and staleness for a given Plan. Only importId enters the Plan (plan.importIds).

observability.description: unobservable: the capture could not observe this subject (no source map, not instrumented); unmapped: no correspondence to an inventoried source path. Neither is ever an unhit signal.

RuntimePayloadV1.description: Payload domain workflow.import-payload.runtime.v1. Its raw canonical bytes hash to wrapper.payloadDigest.

subjects.description: sorted strictly ascending by (path, symbol) UTF-8 bytes

HistoryPayloadV1.description: Payload domain workflow.import-payload.history.v1. Advisory priority input only.

StalenessRule.description: Closed decision table row for staleness classification relative to a Plan's snapshot binding.

condition.description: commit-equal-clean-mapped: commit equal, clean, and an admitted SourceMappingV1 joins every generated path to the Plan snapshot by digest → current/consumable. commit-equal-clean-unmapped: commit and clean flag alone → current/unmapped-only (a commit string cannot prove byte correspondence).

x-opensip-imported-requirement-law.standing: Normative and CLOSED. THE outcome law for a repair EvidenceRequirement whose relation is one of the two imported-evidence relations registered above. It adds no relation, no rung, no import kind, no payload domain and no D9 class, code or exit.
x-opensip-imported-requirement-law.whyItIsOwed: repair.schema.json#/$defs/EvidenceRequirement admits ANY relation that repair_preview's admit_atom admits, which is the thirteen native fact relations OR the two relations in this registry. Native section 4.6 `sufficiency_v2` ranges only over a native VIEW: asked about runtime-observation or history-change it returns `required-relation-missing`, because there is no view entry for a relation that mints no fact2. So a requirement over an imported relation was admissible with no defined producer for its outcome, and the earlier claim that sufficiency_v2 is the ONLY producer of that field was wrong for exactly these two relations.
x-opensip-imported-requirement-law.twoPlanesOneField: The planes are NOT merged. A native requirement carries a DeficiencyV2 member; an imported requirement carries a member of this vocabulary. They are different sets because they name different machinery: DeficiencyV2 speaks of Coverage states, rungs, universes and resolution completeness, none of which an imported observation has. Writing `resolution-incomplete` about a runtime capture, or `import-unmapped-only` about a native view, is a category error and is refused. Which plane applies is decided at ADMISSION from the relation's registry membership - the same place the two planes are already separated by the evidenceDeclarationRule - and never guessed from the value.

evidence-kind-unavailable.meaning: No admitted import of this relation's evidenceKind reaches this Run.
evidence-kind-unavailable.boundTo: the admitted import set of the evidence Run named by RepairPlanDescriptor.evidenceRunId
evidence-kind-unavailable.groundedIn: section 5: an atom over imported evidence must be declared in evidenceUse and REQUIRED evidence absent makes the rule indeterminate.

import-unmapped-only.meaning: An import of the kind exists but is unmapped-only for this Plan.
import-unmapped-only.boundTo: the StalenessRule disposition of that import against this Plan
import-unmapped-only.groundedIn: section 4 StalenessRule: snapshot-differs, commit-differs, commit-equal-dirty and build-identity-differs are unmapped-only, and unmapped-only evidence never feeds a predicate. Explicitly SELECTING a stale import stays the separate IMPORT.STALE_FOR_PLAN request refusal and is not this outcome.

subject-not-observable.meaning: A required target is carried by the runtime payload as `unobservable` or `unmapped`, so the capture made no claim about it in either direction.
subject-not-observable.groundedIn: section 4: unobservable/unmapped never become unhit signals and the schema refuses a hit count on them.

observation-window-insufficient.meaning: A mapped observation exists but its window or population does not meet what the recipe asked for.
observation-window-insufficient.boundTo: RuntimePayloadV1.observationWindow and observedPopulation, compared against the admitted repair recipe's declared demand; the demand is an input, never inferred from the payload
observation-window-insufficient.groundedIn: section 4: positive and bounded-negative runtime evidence is admitted always together with the observation window and population.

history-range-insufficient.meaning: A mapped history import exists but its revision range does not meet what the recipe asked for, or the range was truncated.
history-range-insufficient.groundedIn: HistoryPayloadV1 carries revisionRange with an explicit `truncated` flag and NO observationWindow, observedPopulation or observability. History has its own projection and the runtime one is never applied to it.

history-outside-collection-scope.meaning: A required target lies outside the scope the history collection covered, so its absence from the payload carries no information.
history-outside-collection-scope.groundedIn: collectionScope is a required member precisely so that an absent path can be distinguished from an unexamined one.

import-absent-for-requirement.meaning: The kind is available and consumable and the target was in scope, but the payload carries no subject row reaching that target.
import-absent-for-requirement.groundedIn: the existing IMPORT.ABSENT_FOR_PREDICATE condition, applied per requirement rather than per predicate. Named separately from evidence-kind-unavailable because the remedies differ: import the evidence versus widen the capture.

x-opensip-imported-requirement-law.precedenceRule: Most specific first, in the order a consumer can act on: an absent kind is imported, an unmapped-only import is re-mapped or re-captured against the current snapshot, an unobservable subject is instrumented, an insufficient window is widened, and only then is the observation genuinely silent about the target. Every applicable condition is evaluated; the reported outcome is the first in this order.
x-opensip-imported-requirement-law.whatThisOutcomeNeverEstablishes: No imported observation establishes a universal negative. One window never establishes universal non-use, `observable-unhit` is not `unused`, and runtime coverage is never OpenSIP Coverage. In particular imported evidence can NEVER BY ITSELF establish the native closed world or authorize an unsafe delete or replace: EVERY delete and EVERY replace is decided against the evidence Run's own native ClosedWorldV2 (native section 4.5) before any descriptor exists, and no imported outcome changes deadCodeRepairEligible. It may, however, be an ADDITIONAL required condition alongside an already-established native safety basis - a recipe may lawfully require both - so it is wrong to say imported evidence can never affect applicability. Both directions are held by controls: an unsafe plan whose only requirement is a satisfied imported one is still refused by the closed-world gate, and an unsatisfied imported requirement still makes an otherwise-eligible plan inapplicable.
whatIsPreserved: the original evidence Run named by evidenceRunId remains the authority; nothing here is a substitute for it
per-target evaluation: the outcome is decided against THIS requirement's targets, not against the payload as a whole
observation window and observed population travel with every positive and bounded-negative claim, exactly as section 4 requires
required versus optional stays where evidenceUse already puts it; an optional absence is the existing IMPORT.ABSENT_FOR_PREDICATE disclosure and is not a deficiency
the native sufficiency guard is untouched: sufficiency_v2 still owns every native relation and is not asked about these two
x-opensip-imported-requirement-law.enforcedAt: workflows_model.admit_evidence_requirement decides the plane and refuses a cross-plane value or a shape violation at the repair-preview producer/consumer boundary; workflows_model.imported_requirement_outcome is the reference projection implementing the precedence and the per-kind applicability above, over already-admitted inputs. The vocabulary is mirrored into workflows common as ImportedRequirementDeficiency and held equal to this law.

perKindApplicability.rule: Each relation may report only the outcomes its own payload can ground. A history requirement can never report a runtime observability or window outcome, and a runtime requirement can never report a history range or collection-scope outcome; the producer refuses rather than borrowing the other kind's projection.

inputBinding.standing: EvidenceRequirement carries only relation, minResolution, completeness, satisfied and deficiency. Every other input this law reads is named here with the field that owns it, so no untyped caller value stands in for a measured Run.
inputBinding.targets: RepairPlanDescriptor.targets - the plan's own FINGERPRINTS. They are not a field of EvidenceRequirement and none is added. They are not payload subject keys either: see targetSubjectProjection for the deterministic join through the evidence Run's retained finding and its finding-fingerprint subjectKey, including symbol-versus-file granularity, the disclosed history widening, ambiguity refusal and unmatched handling.
inputBinding.allVersusAny: RepairPlanDescriptor.evidenceRequirements[].completeness. SELECTED CLARIFICATION, and its provenance is recorded accurately: the enum `complete | partial-acceptable` already existed, but its meaning FOR AN IMPORTED REQUIREMENT OVER PLAN TARGETS is chosen here and was not previously published. `complete` requires EVERY target supported; `partial-acceptable` requires at least one. An earlier revision said the enum `already means exactly this`, which was a historical overclaim.
inputBinding.requiredVersusOptional: the owning rule/recipe evidenceUse declaration (workflows section 5), projected by the host into a TYPED BOOLEAN input. The reference REFUSES a non-boolean rather than treating a falsy value as optional, so there is no `unknown` state at this boundary and no default is applied to one. An earlier revision claimed unknown declarations are read as required while accepting None and 0 as optional; the claim is withdrawn and the boundary is typed instead. A repair requirement is NOT automatically identical to policy predicate truth: the policy evaluator's optional-absence route is its own, under its own stated conditions, and this projection is related to the owning declaration rather than equated with that route.
inputBinding.windowDemand: The bounded observation demand is owned by the ADMITTED RECIPE CLOSURE named by RepairPlanDescriptor.recipe.closureId - a content-addressed, signed contribution closure whose current-trust disposition repair preview already resolves and whose revocation already invalidates apply. It is NOT a wire field: RecipeRef carries only contributionId, recipeId, recipeVersion and closureId, and an earlier revision wrongly spoke of `the admitted repair recipe's declared observation demand` as though such a field existed. The host projects the closure-owned deterministic demand into the typed input this reference consumes; the reference does not re-derive it and does not invent one when it is absent.
inputBinding.admittedInputsOnly: This is a PURE reference projection over inputs an authenticated importer and the retained Run closure have ALREADY admitted. It does not itself validate an opaque Run, does not re-derive source correspondence, and does not admit payload, observation scope or polarity - those remain the importer's and the evaluator's. Its preconditions are stated so a caller cannot mistake it for that admission.

x-opensip-imported-requirement-law.whatASatisfiedOutcomeMeans: It means the requirement's evidential condition was met over the BOUND window, range and population - not that the evidence is positive. `observed-hit` is positive execution evidence and `observable-unhit` is BOUNDED NEGATIVE evidence; both can satisfy a requirement, and which one did is carried in the disclosure rather than collapsed. An OPTIONAL absence that satisfies under the evidenceUse rule is satisfied by ABSENCE, not by positive evidence, and its disclosure says so. Calling every satisfied outcome positive would contradict section 4 and would throw away the richer evidence the bounded-negative case exists to carry.

targetSubjectProjection.standing: Normative and CLOSED, and a SELECTED CLARIFICATION rather than a restatement: nothing before this published how a repair target reaches an imported payload subject. It introduces no new record and no new field; it names the retained records that already carry the join.
targetSubjectProjection.theProblemItSolves: RepairPlanDescriptor.targets are FINGERPRINTS - `finding-key2:<64 hex>` - while RuntimeSubject is keyed by {path, symbol?} and HistorySubject by {path}. They are different vocabularies, and an earlier revision read the payload maps DIRECTLY by the target string and called the targets the payload subjects. That silently equated a finding-key identity with a LogicalPath and skipped a real join.
deterministicProjection: 1. TARGET -> FINDING. Every target must be a finding of the evidence Run named by RepairPlanDescriptor.evidenceRunId; repair preview already refuses a target that is not (REQUEST.PRECONDITION_FAILED, `target fingerprint not in the evidence Run`). This is the binding to the ORIGINAL evidence Run and it is not weakened here.

2. FINDING -> FINGERPRINT DESCRIPTOR. The `finding-key2` identity is the H identity of the retained foundation `finding-fingerprint` descriptor, whose retention mode is `preimage`, so its exact bytes are retained under that digest and are re-hashed at Run closure. The projection therefore reads a RETAINED record, never a caller assertion.

3. DESCRIPTOR -> SUBJECT KEY. The retained descriptor carries subjectKey = {language, kind, logicalPath, qualifiedName, discriminator}. The projection reads logicalPath and qualifiedName for payload matching and reports the answer granularity; it does not classify the target using the open kind vocabulary.

4a. RUNTIME MATCH. A RuntimeSubject row matches when its `path` equals `subjectKey.logicalPath` AND, when that row carries `symbol`, its `symbol` equals `subjectKey.qualifiedName` - so a symbol-keyed row for a DIFFERENT symbol never matches. A row with NO symbol is a FILE-level observation: it matches on path but its answerGranularity is `file` and granularityWidenedToFile is true, so a path-only row NEVER silently passes as a symbol-level answer.
4b. HISTORY MATCH. HistorySubject has NO symbol field, so a row matches when its `path` equals `subjectKey.logicalPath`, and every history answer is file-level and reported as such.
5. AMBIGUITY REFUSES. If more than one payload subject matches one target, the projection is not deterministic and the host REFUSES rather than choosing; no silent first-match.
6. UNMATCHED IS UNSUPPORTED. A target with no matching subject is unsupported. It never becomes satisfied, and it is never read as evidence of non-use.
targetSubjectProjection.whatItDoesNotDo: It derives no fact, mints no identity, and admits no payload. It is a READ over records the authenticated importer and the retained Run closure have already admitted, and its result is the already-admitted projection the reference outcome function consumes.
targetSubjectProjection.referenceProjection: workflows_model.project_targets_to_imported_subjects implements steps 1-6 over the retained records and returns the per-target projection that imported_requirement_outcome consumes, so the join is EXERCISED and joined to its caller rather than only described. It refuses `native.imported-projection-ambiguous-target` and `native.imported-projection-target-not-in-evidence-run`.
targetSubjectProjection.granularityIsReportedNotClassified: Every subjectKey carries a qualifiedName, and `subjectKey.kind` has NO closed vocabulary in this contract set, so this projection does NOT classify the target by kind and no kind vocabulary is invented for it. What it reports is the granularity of the ANSWER relative to the key: `answerGranularity` is `symbol` only when a symbol-naming row matched, and `granularityWidenedToFile` marks every file-level answer to a keyed subject. Any coarsening the imported format cannot avoid - history having no symbol field at all, and a runtime capture that emitted only file rows - is therefore stated on the outcome rather than absorbed. This projection adds no capability to either payload format. A symbol-naming row represents only the imported format's path-and-name granularity: neither imported format distinguishes subjectKey.language, kind or discriminator. Different findings may therefore project to the same observation. This uniform projection limitation does not establish execution or non-execution of a particular subject variant beyond the captured granularity; answerGranularity=symbol is not an exact match of the complete subject key.
